policy: Only local fake provider executables and temporary loopback HTTP servers were used. No real provider requests, public relay calls, or secrets.
reproduce_probes: Run from the repository root. QUALIFICATION_ROOT optionally selects an archived baseline source tree with node_modules linked to locally installed dependencies. Example: QUALIFICATION_ROOT=/tmp/baseline node docs/qualification/2026-11-01/evidence/product/qualify-product.mjs

performance.caveat: Small warm-filesystem local measurements; no acceptance threshold or cross-platform claim. At 1000 tasks, event polling rereads 8104000 bytes every nominal 250 ms.

async_spawn.command: node --test --test-name-pattern='EAGAIN|waits for the child spawn' test/node-local.test.mjs test/ui-launch.test.mjs
async_spawn.behavior: Worker start/resume reject asynchronous EAGAIN, UI rejects before health polling, and log descriptors close on failure. Successful worker starts await the spawn event.

scope: This agent fixed worker/runtime launch descriptors and URL paths, UI workspace identity checks, syntax-check error propagation, generated provider onboarding example, and dependency documentation. Parent agent owns task allocation/lifecycle and CLI parsing corrections.
compatibility_limit: No local Node20 binary was available; no download or public registry lookup was performed. Minimum-runtime qualification remains open.

checks: Exactly one opposite live grant admitted
Recovery waits for gated launcher reservation

remaining_limitation.observation: Close an active task, then receive a live ACP permission: task remains done, worker/provider stay alive waiting; allow refuses done and rerun refuses an active execution. Probe terminates its own fixture processes afterward.
remaining_limitation.classification: Operability/resource limitation consistent with declared no-cancellation behavior; no silent permission approval or closure reversal is recommended.

command_worker_crash.severity: P1 if the strict sequential execution claim covers worker crashes
command_worker_crash.expected: Recovery/rerun confirms the previous provider execution tree has stopped, or refuses rerun with orphan-execution guidance.
command_worker_crash.actual: SIGKILL stops the worker but leaves its silent command child alive and writing. Recovery marks failed/crashed. Rerun starts a second provider while the first continues writing.
command_worker_crash.cleanup: Both recorded workers and both recorded command-provider processes were explicitly terminated and verified dead.
remedy_options: Record and validate local process-group ownership, verify or quiesce the owned group before rerun, and fail closed when ownership cannot be established; platform-specific work is required.
Use a surviving per-run supervisor/watchdog to own and tear down the provider process tree when the worker dies.
command_worker_crash.insufficient_remedy: Adding command-provider cancel() only helps graceful termination; a worker killed with SIGKILL cannot run cancellation code.

resolution.status: Rerun admission is now guarded for recorded local POSIX execution groups. Recovery records the orchestration failure and does not kill saved process identities.

saved_session_orphan_resume.pre_fix_observation: A fake native CLI left a same-group heartbeat descendant after publishing a saved-session permission. Non-live allow started another session while that descendant remained alive.
saved_session_orphan_resume.resolution: The shared process-group admission guard now runs before non-live resume clears old ownership. Live in-place permission grants remain exempt.
remaining_scope: POSIX only; Windows process-tree ownership remains unqualified.
Protects newly recorded local execution groups; a descendant that deliberately starts a different process group can escape this guard.
Legacy task records without processGroupId cannot be retroactively assigned verified process-group ownership.
Numeric identity reuse may conservatively refuse admission; saved process/group IDs are never automatically killed.
saved_session_orphan_resume.cleanup: Every fixture worker and recorded provider PID is individually terminated and verified dead by test cleanup.

pty_terminal_worker_diagnostic.observed_flash: Task #1 still has execution processes in local process group 79255. Inspect and stop the previous execution before continuing.
pty_terminal_worker_diagnostic.observation: Only the terminal worker remained in its group, still alive through more than600ms; provider had already exited. The250ms group admission grace expired.
pty_terminal_worker_diagnostic.source_cause: ACP shutdown unconditionally schedules a referenced2000ms timer, including from child close after the child is already dead. The close path does not clear the timer when the run has already settled.
pty_terminal_worker_diagnostic.proposed_remedy: Clear the ACP shutdown timer on actual child close and avoid scheduling cleanup for an already-closed child. Preserve the process-group guard.

resolution.review: ACP shutdown now skips an already-closed child; close clears shutdownTimer and pending RPC timers before returning for settled runs.
resolution.timing_caveat: Observed timestamps from this diagnostic only; no wall-clock acceptance threshold is asserted.
